name: WA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +22-point partisan lean
Longtime incumbent Adam Smith with a large fundraising advantage
Challenger Doug Basler raised only about $12,000 with no outside support
Prediction markets price the Democrat at roughly 97%
model.rationale: Adam Smith is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by 22 points, while Doug Basler has raised almost nothing and drawn no outside spending. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy incumbent win, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin of about 26 points.
model.watch: A major late infusion of outside money for Basler or an unexpected incumbent scandal would be the main things to move this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Washington's 9th District is a solidly Democratic seat, leaning 22 points Democratic, and Adam Smith has held it for decades. He is running again and has raised about $1.9 million with nearly $870,000 on hand, while Republican challenger Doug Basler has raised roughly $12,000 and has no outside support on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price Smith's chances near 97%. Everything points to a comfortable Smith victory, with the only real uncertainty being the exact size of the margin.
